newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks extend gains on "dual" sector rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks extend gains on "dual" sector rise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices extended early gains in late Thursday trade as electronics and financials both rose strongly to lead the upswing in a rare phenomemon that brokers have dubbed "dual mainstreaming".
With 60 minutes left, at 0300 GMT, the index was up 120.58 points or 1.29 percent to 9,483.26, a new seven-year intraday high. Turnover was a heavy T$143 billion.
Brokers noted a rare instance in which two most heavily weighted sectors -- financials and electronics -- were strong at the same time.
"When you see this dual mainstreaming, both sectors rising at the same time, you know how bullish the market is now," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.
Financials were up 1.89 percent, with China Development up T$8 to T$163.

Electronics were up 1.71 percent, with No.2 microchip maker United Microelectronics up T$5 to T$141.5 after giving a senior post to Donald Brooks, who until April was president of No.1 arch rival Taiwan Semiconductor.
Brokers said the index would test 9,500-9,600 resistance soon, but said they worried about the central bank's policy.
"If turnover breaks the all-time-high T$251 billion, the central bank may take tougher moves to tighten liquidity," Yang said.
